learn.title: Brackets first
learn.body: A number outside brackets multiplies everything inside. This is the distributive rule: $2(x+3)=2x+6$. Remove the brackets, then solve the equation as usual.

learn.title: Solve $3(x-2)+5=2x+4$
learn.body: Distribute, tidy up, then gather the $x$ terms.

learn.title: Clearing fractions
learn.body: Fractions are easier to remove than to carry around. Multiply every term on both sides by a number all the denominators divide into, such as 6 for halves and thirds.
Multiply every single term, not just one. A common slip is to multiply the fraction but forget the whole number on the other side.

questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 3: $x+2=5$, so $x=3$. Or distribute first: $3x+6=15$, $3x=9$.
The 2 multiplies every term inside the brackets, so $2\cdot4=8$.
Multiply both sides by 4 to undo the division: $x=12$.

questions.prompt: To clear the fractions in $\frac{x}{2}+\frac{x}{3}=5$, multiply every term by
questions.explanation: 6 is the smallest number that both 2 and 3 divide into, so both fractions disappear.

questions.prompt: Solve $2(x+1)=3x-4$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Remove the brackets first, then gather the letters, then finish. Check: $2(7)=14$ and $3\cdot6-4=14$.
Multiply both sides by 2: $x+3=2x-2$. Subtract $x$ and add 2: $5=x$. Check: $4=4$.
